page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-lc1m1.small is an entry-level, burstable virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features a single vCPU mapped to one physical core on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 1.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include any local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supporting instruction set extensions such as AVX, AVX-512, and AES cryptography.

Benchmark data indicates constrained performance across compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core CPU test yielded a score of 1064.79, placing it in the bottom 25% of tested servers, while the multi-core score remained identical due to the single-thread limitation, placing it in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show 76.47 GB/sec for cached small blocks and drop to 8.43 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Passmark CPU and memory scores fall into the bottom 10% tier, reflecting the burstable nature and resource constraints of the hardware profile.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its burstable CPU allocation and low baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps, which limits sustained high-throughput operations. However, it offers qualitative cost efficiency for lightweight, intermittent workloads that do not require continuous CPU utilization. Appropriate workloads include basic static web serving, which achieved a throughput of 1.28 GB/sec in testing, simple Redis caching operations with 1.34 million operations per second, microservices, and low-traffic development or testing environments.
